WIC7A-01.deciding_sentence: adjacent (sentence after: large share along rows / almost none across)
WIC7A-01.note: Clean. Once the next sentence is read the answer is mechanical; medium is generous, easy-medium on the hard route. 'negligible' reappears as the key in A-04.

WIC7A-02.deciding_sentence: further away (sentence 2: 'asked to find cracks that are already large enough to be found'); sentence 3 kills the strong distractor 'a vindication'
WIC7A-02.note: 'a vindication' is a genuinely strong distractor and the kill ('A find does not confirm the schedule') is direct. The 'formality' kill is soft: 'chosen so that such a crack will be caught' shows the inspection matters, but 'a formality' is a poor fit for a crack find on its own, so the option dies on sense, not on that sentence. Keep.

WIC7A-03.read_aloud_flag: stilted completion: 'as a forecast ... it is insufficient' is an odd collocation; the natural word is optimistic/unreliable, which is not offered
WIC7A-03.deciding_sentence: further away (sentence 4: 'the shelf loss dominates ... exhausted after a few hundred')
WIC7A-03.note: The 'though' contrast separates the ceiling role from the forecast role, so the 'mute' kill ('still holds as a ceiling') addresses the wrong role: a rating can bound life and still say nothing about grid life as a forecast. The 'still holds as a ceiling' clause bounds, so 'mute' is overstated and loses, but a careful student can argue it for a while. HOLD for key wording; 'insufficient' reads as filler.

WIC7A-04.note: Blank sentence decides it via 'but'. Fine as an easy anchor; not a module-2 hard item.

WIC7A-05.deciding_sentence: further away (sentence 2 'reads as one year short' plus sentence 4 'absent from one is present in the rest')
WIC7A-05.note: Two sentences combine; neither alone. Clean. 'impossible' is a throwaway.

WIC7A-06.read_aloud_flag: format tell: key is the only bare noun; the three distractors all carry an article ('an instrument', 'an anomaly', 'a malfunction')
WIC7A-06.deciding_sentence: further away (sentence 2: 'filter it out ... since a small event is lost beneath it')
WIC7A-06.note: 'an instrument' is the good trap (it is what the researchers made of the hum, and the blank asks about the networks). Distractor pair anomaly/malfunction are both 'something wrong' and a student strikes them together. The article asymmetry is a visible oddity in the option list; consider a mass-noun distractor (e.g. 'interference' would be too close; 'static'? also too close) or accept it.

WIC7A-07.deciding_sentence: further away for the key (sentence 2, yield); adjacent (sentence 3, same speed) kills the strong distractor 'fast'
WIC7A-07.note: 'elegant' and 'versatile' are killed by absence only; the cited sentence supports the key rather than contradicting them. The student must also supply yield -> cost, since 'cost' never appears. Acceptable inference but note the key is not lexically anchored.

WIC7A-08.note: The colon decides it. 'coarse' kill is a precision argument, not a contradiction. Easy.

WIC7A-09.deciding_sentence: adjacent (sentence 3: 'spread these genes at a speed nothing in the Pleistocene could match')
WIC7A-09.note: 'detect' is a mild trap (overuse revealed resistance) but the passage says overuse spread it. Clean.

WIC7A-10.deciding_sentence: further away (sentence 2: 'dismissed as evidence of careless mixing')
WIC7A-10.note: Near-paraphrase of the passage; 'defect' is the only option compatible with 'dismissed ... careless'. Easy, not medium. Useful variety: here the OLD view's word is the key (see cross-item note).

WIC7A-11.my_answer: indecisive (with misleading as a live alternative)
WIC7A-11.read_aloud_flag: distractor near-synonym pair: redundant / gratuitous are struck together, leaving a two-way choice
WIC7A-11.deciding_sentence: adjacent (the 'But' rebuttal after the blank); sentence 1 'a single commitment' is the anchor for 'indecisive'
WIC7A-11.note: DROP or revise. The blank is what CRITICS call the practice, so the 'misleading' kill (sentence 3 shows the spread is informative) proves the critics wrong, not that they did not say it; only the rebuttal's shape constrains the blank. The rebuttal is two-pronged: 'never the commitment it appeared to be' answers 'indecisive', but the closing 'conceals that it has done so' is a tu-quoque answer to 'misleading' (the single number was the misleading one). With redundant/gratuitous struck as a pair, the student faces indecisive vs misleading and both survive. Fix would be to cut 'and conceals that it has done so' and lean the rebuttal wholly on commitment, then re-attack; otherwise drop.

WIC7A-12.deciding_sentence: adjacent (sentence 3: 'not in how few bits are added but in which of the message's bits each one watches')
WIC7A-12.note: 'rather than brute' narrows to an antonym of brute; sentence 3 then picks 'structured'. 'uniform' kill is real (checks must differ). Clean; medium-hard.

WIC7A-13.deciding_sentence: blank's own (tail: 'a faint pattern laid over the ordinary image of the sky'; 'image' sits five words past the blank)
WIC7A-13.note: The blank sentence's own tail decides it, and 'retina' in the sentence before makes it trivial. Easy.

WIC7A-14.read_aloud_flag: homograph: 'suspended' in a sediment passage reads first as 'suspended sediment/in suspension'; a student may pick it for the wrong sense or avoid it as a pun
WIC7A-14.deciding_sentence: further away (sentences 3-4: 'not gone', 'passed through the gates in controlled releases')
WIC7A-14.note: 'destroyed' is the tempting first read and is killed cleanly by 'not gone'. 'diverted' kill is fair (held in the river's own basin). Keep; the homograph is a wobble, not a leak.

WIC7B-01.read_aloud_flag: passage length ~150 words, at the ceiling for SAT R&W and long for WIC
WIC7B-01.deciding_sentence: further away (sentences 2-3: letters are about roads; 'the loss the writers count is the coin they would otherwise have sent')
WIC7B-01.note: 'evasion' is the received view and a strong trap; killed directly by the usury sentence. 'speculation' killed by 'known in advance'. Good hard item. Received-view word is a distractor (cross-item pattern).

WIC7B-02.deciding_sentence: further away (sentence 2: 'each new name chiselled over the last ... as though the newcomer had laid the road himself')
WIC7B-02.note: 'old ones' right after the blank kills 'extending' for free. 'commemorating' survives a student who reads a milestone as a memorial; the kill relies on inferring that over-cutting predecessors is erasure not honour, which is right but is an inference, not a contradiction. Keep.

WIC7B-03.read_aloud_flag: 'the usual precipice' semantically baits 'habit'; 'suspended' in this passage is the key of A-14 (cross-item only)
WIC7B-03.deciding_sentence: adjacent (sentence 4: asks to spare it, 'is told it may not')
WIC7B-03.note: 'design' is the critics' word (received view) and is killed by the revision sentence; 'habit' is baited by 'usual' and killed by the request/refusal. Clean; the refusal decides it.

WIC7B-04.read_aloud_flag: 'convenience' is a relative of 'conveniently' in sentence 1 (the received view); passage ~150 words
WIC7B-04.deciding_sentence: adjacent (sentence 4: 'The forms that finally became fixed are the ones in those tables ... it was the printing house that gave way')
WIC7B-04.note: 'of the schoolroom' after the blank plus sentence 4 decide it. 'concession' kill ('the printing house gave way') is direct. The lexical relative 'convenience'/'conveniently' points at the rejected view, so it works as a trap for the skimmer rather than as a giveaway; note but keep. a(n) is balanced (two vowel, two consonant options).

WIC7B-05.read_aloud_flag: ambiguity: 'protective' also reads as protectionist (protecting the guild), i.e. the REJECTED view; a student who buys the received view picks the key for the wrong reason, and one who rejects it may strike 'protective' as a synonym of 'exclusionary'
WIC7B-05.deciding_sentence: further away (sentences 3-4: refused only substandard metal; fines paid doubled to the buyer)
WIC7B-05.note: Key is right (protective of the buyer) and every kill is direct, but the key's second sense overlaps the main distractor. Consider 'a consumer safeguard'-type phrasing or keep as is with the risk noted.

WIC7B-06.deciding_sentence: adjacent (sentence 2: letters 'ask for particular embellishments by name')
WIC7B-06.note: The letters clause decides it and kills compromise and rebuke at once; the 'first section in detail' contrast kills oversight. Rated hard in the batch; on the hard route this is medium because the letters clause is explicit.

WIC7B-08.read_aloud_flag: cross-item only: B-04's passage opens 'The settling of English spelling'
WIC7B-08.deciding_sentence: adjacent (sentence 3: 'narrowing to the table only later, in the mouths of speakers who had no lords to please')
WIC7B-08.note: 'over generations' after the blank already kills 'imposed ... at a single moment'; sentence 3 does the rest. 'imposed' is the received-view word. Clean.

WIC7B-09.read_aloud_flag: option 'credit' is a word in the passage ('ended the month with a small credit'); deliberate trap but a lexical relative under the rule
WIC7B-09.deciding_sentence: adjacent (sentence after: 'could not buy a train ticket')
WIC7B-09.note: The train-ticket sentence hands over the answer; on the hard route this is easy despite the batch's 'medium'. Keep.

WIC7B-10.deciding_sentence: blank's own ('A stump ... told a visitor that the statue reproduced a famous bronze, and the copy's value lay in its ___')
WIC7B-10.note: The blank's own first clause decides it; the passage is needed only to kill material/workmanship/pose, and all three kills are direct quotes. 'pedigree' is figurative vocabulary and the earned difficulty. Good item.

WIC7B-11.deciding_sentence: further away (sentence 1 'described as mercy' sets the term the blank must echo; sentence 2 supplies the refutation)
WIC7B-11.note: 'less a(n) ___ than a procedure' must echo the received view (mercy) and 'reprieve' is the only option that does. Here the received-view word is the KEY, a welcome inversion of the batch's dominant pattern. 'punishment' kill is right: sanctuary punished, so 'less a punishment' contradicts. Vocabulary carries the difficulty.

WIC7B-12.deciding_sentence: adjacent (sentence 5: 'they ask that the maxima be cut ... Parliament had moved it upward every time')
WIC7B-12.note: 'unequal' is the received-view word and killed by the petition evidence; 'discretionary' killed by 'stood where the act had put it'. Clean but the passage is dense for one word; medium.

WIC7B-13.deciding_sentence: adjacent (sentence 3: 'a listener who had missed a night could find the place at which to rejoin')
WIC7B-13.note: 'preview' (received view) killed by 'passed over the heading'; 'joke' by 'grave chapters as evenly'. Clean.

WIC7B-14.read_aloud_flag: cross-item only: 'mute' is a distractor in A-03
WIC7B-14.deciding_sentence: adjacent (sentence 4: 'they felt it at one remove, and the rise was smaller')
WIC7B-14.note: 'undetectable' is the real trap (remote markets 'recorded nothing at all') and is killed by 'their prices rose'; 'delayed' is killed only by absence, hence partial. Keep.

drops.WIC7A-11: not exclusive: 'misleading' survives; the blank is the critics' term so the cited kill (the practice is in fact informative) does not reach it, and the rebuttal's closing clause 'conceals that it has done so' answers 'misleading' as well as 'indecisive'. Distractors redundant/gratuitous are a near-synonym pair struck together, leaving a coin flip.

holds.WIC7A-03: key 'insufficient' is a stilted completion for 'as a forecast ... it is'; 'mute' is weakly defensible because the 'though' contrast separates the ceiling role from the forecast role and the kill quotes the ceiling role. Re-key with a natural word (optimistic/unreliable) and re-attack rather than ship.

cross_item_tells: Received-view distractor: in 11 of 27 items the option naming the opening 'received view' is a distractor (B-01 evasion, B-03 design, B-04 convenience, B-05 exclusionary, B-08 imposed, B-10 material, B-12 unequal, B-13 preview, A-06 an instrument [inverted: it is the NEW view], A-09 none, A-11 none). A student who strikes 'the word the passage set up to knock down' gets one free elimination per item. Three items invert it (A-10 'a defect', B-11 'reprieve', A-11's blank IS the critics' word), which is enough to stop it being a rule but not enough to stop it being a strategy. Author more inversions in the next batch.
Key letter: slot A holds 12 of 27 keys (44%), D holds 3. If insert does not shuffle, this alone trips verify-answer-key-spread.

Argument shape: 20 of 27 passages are 'X is usually read as P; the records show Q; blank = Q'. Every B item and A-06/A-09/A-10/A-11 follow it. Not a leak by itself but it makes the blank's polarity predictable from sentence 1.
Passage length: B-01, B-04, B-05, B-12 run 130-150 words, at or over the SAT R&W ceiling and well over the typical WIC length; four items in one cohort makes the batch look non-SAT on the page.

Word recurrence across items: negligible (A-01 distractor, A-04 key), mute/muted (A-03 distractor, B-14 key), suspended (A-14 key, B-03 passage), settled/settling (B-08 key, B-04 passage). None within an item; harmless unless two land on one form.
